answer: An equivocation slash stops one operator running many faces: an identity filing two conflicting proofs in one epoch loses 30 of its 100-credit bond and freezes for one epoch. Each proof carries a yarrow tag bound to one key, so a second proof under the same tag shows on the ledger. A sparrow audit checks 5% of identities each epoch and triggers the slash on any mismatch. The named failure mode is proof-splitting: the k-th fake needs its own 100-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits, none reusable. An honest agent posts one bond and keeps a haven of full weight.
